## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of end-to-end CD basics: source → build → test → containerize → push → deploy with kubectl; environment-specific config and secrets integration; security gates and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines
- Azure Container Registry (ACR)
- AKS deployment via kubectl
- Azure App Configuration for per-environment settings
- Azure Key Vault for secrets
- Image vulnerability scanning gate
- Post-deploy health checks and rollback
- Logging to Azure Monitor Logs

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
- main
pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
steps:
- task: NodeTool@0
  inputs:
    versionSpec: '16.x'
- script: |
    npm ci
    npm test
  displayName: 'Install and test'
- task: Docker@2
  inputs:
    containerRegistry: '$(ACRServiceConnection)'
    repository: 'node-api'
    command: 'buildAndPush'
    Dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
    tags: |
      $(Build.BuildId)
- task: Kubernetes@1
  inputs:
    connectionType: 'Azure Resource Manager'
    azureSubscription: '$(AZ_SUBSCRIPTION)'
    azureResourceGroup: 'rg'
    kubernetesCluster: 'cluster'
    namespace: 'default'
    command: 'apply'
    useConfigurationFile: true
    configuration: |
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: node-api
      spec:
        replicas: 1
        template:
          spec:
            containers:
            - name: node-api
              image: <ACR>/node-api:$(Build.BuildId)
              ports:
              - containerPort: 3000
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this for multi-tenant deployments with per-tenant namespaces?
- How would you implement a manual approval gate before production deployment?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests a realistic, beginner-friendly pipeline that covers core Azure DevOps tasks: CI, Docker, ACR, App Service slots, App Configuration integration, health-based swap, and Log Analytics auditing.

## Key Concepts

- YAML pipelines and multi-stage design
- Docker build/push to Azure Container Registry
- Azure App Service deployment slots (staging/production) and slot swap
- Azure App Configuration for per-environment flags
- Health checks and rollback strategies
- Logging/auditing to Azure Monitor / Log Analytics
- Service connections and least-privilege access

## Code Example

```yaml
trigger:
- main
pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest
variables:
  imageName: myapi
  registry: <ACR_NAME>.azurecr.io
stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: Test
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs: {version: '18.x'}
    - script: npm install
    - script: npm test
- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - job: Deploy
    steps:
    - task: Docker@2
      inputs:
        command: buildAndPush
        containerRegistry: '<registry-service-connection>'
        repository: '$(registry)/$(imageName)'
        Dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
        tags: |
          $(Build.BuildId)
    - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '<subscription-connection>'
        appName: '<app-service-name>'
        imageName: '$(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)'
        resourceGroup: '<rg>'
        slotName: 'staging'
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '<subscription-connection>'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        script: |
          HEALTH_URL=https://<app-service-name>-staging.azurewebsites.net/health
          if curl -sSf $HEALTH_URL | grep -q 'ok'; then
            az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app-service-name> --slot staging --target-slot production
          else
            az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app-service-name> --slot production --target-slot staging
            exit 1
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you add a retry policy for the health check without masking failures?
- How would you extend this to support a blue/green rollout for multiple regions?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design a CI/CD pipeline that enforces governance gates before deployment while enabling rapid feedback through ephemeral environments.

## Key Concepts
- Azure Policy integration as a CI/CD gate
- AKS ephemeral namespace deployment
- Helm-based deployments with per-environment configuration
- Azure Key Vault and Azure App Configuration integration
- Health checks and automatic rollback mechanisms
- Azure Monitor logging for traceability

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
pr: none

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndTest
        pool:
          vmImage: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '20.x'
          - script: npm install && npm test
  
  - stage: PolicyCheck
    jobs:
      - job: AKSComplianceCheck
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
              script: |
                az policy state list \
                  --resource-group $(AKS_RESOURCE_GROUP) \
                  --filter "complianceState eq 'NonCompliant'"
  
  - stage: Deploy
    dependsOn: PolicyCheck
    jobs:
      - job: DeployToEphemeralNS
        steps:
          - task: HelmInstaller@1
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            script: |
              NAMESPACE="pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)"
              helm upgrade --install $NAMESPACE ./chart \
                --namespace $NAMESPACE --create-namespace \
                --set env=$(DEPLOYMENT_ENV)
  
  - stage: Validate
    jobs:
      - job: HealthCheck
        steps:
          - script: |
              curl -f http://$NAMESPACE.health || exit 1
      - job: RollbackOnFailure
        condition: failed()
        steps:
          - script: helm uninstall $NAMESPACE
```

## Why This Question Matters

This question assesses practical Azure DevOps pipeline design skills for per-tenant blue/green deployments with dynamic traffic routing and risk mitigation.

## Key Concepts

- Per-tenant deployment slots in Azure App Service
- Azure Front Door per-tenant routing rules for traffic steering
- Feature flags in App Configuration for controlling new behavior
- Synthetic end-to-end tests and health checks
- Automated rollback mechanisms and guardrails
- Centralized logging with Azure Monitor

## Solution Approach

1. **Deploy to Blue Slots**: Deploy each tenant's updated code to their dedicated blue deployment slot.

2. **Run Synthetic Tests**: Execute per-tenant synthetic tests against the blue deployment to validate functionality.

3. **Traffic Shift**: If all tenants pass, gradually shift traffic from green to blue slots using Azure Front Door's weighted routing (0-100%).

4. **Health Verification**: Monitor health checks post-traffic shift before promoting to production.

5. **Slot Swap**: Swap blue and green slots to promote the new version to production.

6. **Rollback**: If any tenant fails, revert traffic in Azure Front Door and swap slots to restore the previous state.

7. **Logging**: Stream all pipeline steps to Azure Monitor Logs for audit and troubleshooting.

## Why This Is Asked
This question validates the ability to combine per-tenant isolation, cost governance, and centralized telemetry management within a single automated pipeline with built-in rollback capabilities.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant resource scoping with dedicated resource groups, App Configuration, and Key Vault
- Tenant-specific App Service slots with isolated configuration
- Real-time cost forecasting and governance via Azure Cost Management
- Telemetry segregation using tenant-scoped Log Analytics workspaces
- Drift detection and automated rollback strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Azure DevOps YAML Pipeline for Multi-Tenant Onboarding
trigger: none
pr: none

parameters:
  - name: tenantId
    type: string
  - name: tenantName
    type: string
  - name: costThresholdUSD
    type: number
    default: 500

stages:
  - stage: PreValidation
    jobs:
      - job: CostForecastGate
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: CheckCostForecast
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                # Query Cost Management for 30-day forecast
                COST=$(az cost management query \
                  --scope /subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID \
                  --query "properties[0].columns[?(@.name=='Cost')].rows[0]" \
                  --timeframe ThisMonth \
                  --dataset-name CurrentMonth \
                  -o tsv)
                
                PROJECTED=$(( COST * 30 / $(date +%d) ))
                
                if [ $PROJECTED -gt ${{ parameters.costThresholdUSD }} ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Projected cost \$$PROJECTED exceeds threshold \$${{ parameters.costThresholdUSD }}"
                  exit 1
                fi

  - stage: ProvisionResources
    dependsOn: PreValidation
    jobs:
      - job: CreateTenantResources
        steps:
          - task: AzureResourceGroupDeployment@3
            name: ProvisionRG
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              resourceGroupName: 'rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }}'
              location: 'East US'
              templateLocation: 'Inline'
              mode: 'Incremental'

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: ProvisionAppConfig
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                az appconfig create \
                  --name "appconfig-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --resource-group "rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --location "East US"

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: ProvisionKeyVault
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                az keyvault create \
                  --name "kv-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --resource-group "rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --location "East US"

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: CreateLogAnalytics
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                az monitor log-analytics workspace create \
                  --workspace-name "la-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --resource-group "rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" \
                  --location "East US"

  - stage: DeployAppService
    dependsOn: ProvisionResources
    jobs:
      - job: DeploySlot
        steps:
          - task: AzureAppServiceSettings@1
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              appName: 'saas-api-${{ parameters.tenantName }}'
              slotName: 'staging'
              appSettings: |
                TENANT_ID=${{ parameters.tenantId }}
                APP_CONFIG_ENDPOINT=https://appconfig-${{ parameters.tenantName }}.azconfig.io
                KEY_VAULT_URI=https://kv-${{ parameters.tenantName }}.vault.azure.net/
                LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACE_ID=$(az monitor log-analytics workspace show --workspace-name la-${{ parameters.tenantName }} --resource-group rg-${{ parameters.tenantName }} --query customerId -o tsv)

          - task: AzureAppServiceManage@0
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              Action: 'Swap Slots'
              WebAppName: 'saas-api-${{ parameters.tenantName }}'
              SourceSlot: 'staging'

  - stage: ValidateAndMonitor
    dependsOn: DeployAppService
    jobs:
      - job: HealthCheck
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: VerifyTenantAccess
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'Azure-SP-Naming-Conv'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                # Verify Key Vault access policy and App Configuration keys
                az keyvault secret list --vault-name "kv-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" | jq 'length'
                az appconfig kv list --name "appconfig-${{ parameters.tenantName }}" | jq 'length'

          - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
            inputs:
              targetPath: '$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)'
              artifact: 'tenant-config-${{ parameters.tenantId }}'
```

## Testing Strategy
1. **Unit Testing**: Validate ARM template outputs and Bicep configurations with Az CLI dry-run
2. **Integration Testing**: Verify cost gate logic with mocked Cost Management responses
3. **E2E Testing**: Spin up a test tenant and validate resource provisioning, slot deployment, and telemetry routing
4. **Chaos Testing**: Simulate cost threshold exceeded scenarios to confirm pipeline blocks deployment
5. **Compliance Testing**: Ensure tenant resources are properly isolated with RBAC validation

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
  - main

variables:
  azureServiceConnection: 'azure-sp'
  functionAppName: 'my-function-app'
  appConfigName: 'my-app-config'
  keyVaultName: 'my-key-vault'

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: Build
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '18.x'
          - script: npm install
          - script: npm run build
          - publish: $(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/dist
            artifact: drop

  - stage: Test_Audit
    dependsOn: Build
    jobs:
      - job: Test_and_Lint
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '18.x'
          - script: npm install
          - script: npm run lint
          - script: npm test
      - job: Security_Audit
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '18.x'
          - script: npm install
          - script: npm audit --audit-level=moderate

  - stage: Deploy_Staging
    dependsOn: Test_Audit
    variables:
      environment: 'staging'
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployToStaging
        environment: 'staging'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: AzureKeyVault@1
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
                    KeyVaultName: $(keyVaultName)
                    SecretsFilter: '*'
                - task: AzureAppConfiguration@1
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
                    AppConfigurationEndpoint: 'https://$(appConfigName).azconfig.io'
                    labels: 'staging'
                - task: AzureFunctionApp@1
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
                    appType: 'functionApp'
                    appName: $(functionAppName)
                    deploySlot: true
                    slotName: 'staging'
                    package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/dist/*.zip'

  - stage: Load_Test
    dependsOn: Deploy_Staging
    jobs:
      - job: Run_k6
        steps:
          - task: k6LoadTest@1
            inputs:
              filePath: 'tests/load-test.js'
             vus: '50'
              duration: '30s'
              threshold: 'p95=1200,error_rate=1'

  - stage: Promote_or_Rollback
    dependsOn: Load_Test
    jobs:
      - job: Check_conditions
        steps:
          - task: PowerShell@2
            inputs:
              targetType: 'inline'
              script: |
                $metrics = @{
                  p95Latency = 1150
                  errorRate = 0.5
                }
                if ($metrics.p95Latency -lt 1200 -and $metrics.errorRate -lt 1) {
                  Write-Host "Promoting to production"
                } else {
                  Write-Host "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Promote conditions not met"
                  exit 1
                }
      - job: Promote_to_Production
        dependsOn: Check_conditions
        condition: succeeded()
        steps:
          - task: AzureFunctionApp@1
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              appType: 'functionApp'
              appName: $(functionAppName)
              deploySlot: true
              slotName: 'staging'
              swapWithProduction: true
      - job: Rollback_on_Failure
        dependsOn: Check_conditions
        condition: failed()
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az functionApp deployment slot swap \
                  --resource-group my-rg \
                  --name $(functionAppName) \
                  --slot staging \
                  --target-slot production
          - task: AzureMonitor@1
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              alertsToSearch: 'all'
              insightsToSearch: 'all'
```
